column4: annotation

Preprint (465 near-complete assemblies, all-vs-all ends): pseudo-homolog regions on 41/48 arms grouped into sequence communities; claims putative non-homologous subtelomere recombination in a 3-generation T2T pedigree and frames ends as concertedly evolving. The direct target of our re-evaluation.

Preprint: complete subtelomeres for all non-acrocentric arms from 860 haploid assemblies; 21/39 autosomal arms carry multiple haplotypes differing by 100-200 kb, block diversity tracks arm not ancestry, blocks conserved in great apes, rare recombination; also used for end-specific telomere length. Closest prior population catalogue to our atlas.

Data deposit (Zenodo) accompanying the 2026 'Widespread structural variations at human chromosome ends' preprint: human subtelomere sequence collection. Existing public subtelomere sequence resource that our release must be compared against.

Preprint: 316,146 telomere-spanning molecules over 12,080 end-resolved arrays from 212 individuals; proximal TVR codes heritable and arm-specific, influenced by TAR1; reports rare germline interchromosomal telomere exchange. Key comparator for cis telomere and terminal-exchange claims.

Preprint (TeloXplorer): end- and haplotype-resolved telomere length, TVR and methylation; end-specific length rankings conserved across 232 HPRC individuals and 28 populations; extensive interchromosomal sharing of TVR architectures. Directly overlaps cis-length questions on the same cohort.

Combined PacBio/ONT allele-specific telomere length in families; telomere variant sequences are heritable and CRISPR deletion of them resets allele length, arguing that proximal sequence is a causal cis determinant.

Preprint: HiFi telomere lengths in 75 trios; arm-specific lengths consistent between parents and children, TVR-based allele tracing for ~50% of telomeres, paternal alleles longer. Evidence that allele/arm length is inherited.

Telomere Profiling (nanopore): chromosome end-specific and haplotype-specific length distributions; specific ends consistently short or long across 147 individuals. Establishes end-specific length as a population-level property.

STELA at 2p, 11q, 12q, 17p, XpYp: 17p consistently shortest and more stable; hTERT overexpression homogenises lengths. Foundational evidence for cis-acting determinants of chromosome-specific telomere length.
Introduces STELA; extensive allelic variation in single-telomere length and ultrashort telomeres at senescence.
Q-FISH in monozygotic twins: relative lengths of individual telomeres are set in the zygote and maintained through life.
Allelic relative telomere lengths compared over 31 parent-child transmissions segregate in families; early evidence that length is an allele-linked inherited trait.
Q-FISH shows 17p telomeres are consistently short in humans; first chromosome-arm-specific length pattern.
Q-FISH with PNA probes: up to six-fold telomere length heterogeneity within a metaphase; method basis for arm-specific length.
Q-FISH shows homologous chromosomes differ in telomere length and arm-specific patterns are individual-specific and inherited.
Long-read analysis of telomeric haplotypes and variant-repeat heterogeneity; shows telomeres carry arm/haplotype-specific sequence structure.
Xp/Yp telomere-adjacent haplotypes in strong LD; telomere variant-repeat maps reveal allelic turnover mechanisms at the proximal telomere.
Yeast nanopore telomere tagging: chromosome end-specific lengths stable over 120 divisions; proposes minimal functional telomere.
Telobait capture with PacBio HiFi for nucleotide-resolution individual telomere length.
Telogator: chromosome-specific telomere length from long reads by anchoring to subtelomere reference.
Telogator2: identifies all 92 telomere alleles from long reads using TVRs and estimates allele-specific length; principal open tool for per-allele length.
Telo-seq (native ONT): bulk, arm- and allele-specific telomere lengths; resolves shortening in five-population-doubling increments.
Documents systematic nanopore basecalling errors in telomere repeats (TTAGGG miscalled) and correction; a caveat for ONT telomere calls.
Preprint benchmark of TECAT vs Telogator for chromosome end-specific telomere analysis.
Topsicle: k-mer/change-point telomere length estimation from long reads.
TARPON: best-practice nanopore pipeline for arm-specific telomere length with validation focus.
Preprint protocol for nanopore chromosome end-specific telomere length in human cells.
Preprint: high-coverage nanopore WGS shows chromosome-specific telomere length architecture conserved across tissues and populations.
Bionano CRISPR-labelled optical maps give subtelomere-haplotype-resolved telomere length on single molecules.
Optical mapping of terminal segments links subtelomeric variants and long-range haplotypes to specific telomeres; proof of principle for haplotype-linked telomere length and cis elements.

Optical maps of 154 genomes from 26 populations catalogue long-range subtelomere haplotypes and duplicon frequencies per arm, with arm- and population-specific trends and a dated spread of duplicon blocks. Pre-assembly population catalogue of subtelomere alleles.
Subtelomere assemblies for 41 telomere regions; 20.66 Mb analysed, 114 internal (TTAGGG)n-like islands, enrichment >25-fold of ITS. Foundational reference-era subtelomere resource.
Review of human subtelomere structure: recently shuffled duplicated segments and allelic variation.

Systematic duplicon analysis: subtelomeric repeats are ~80% of the distal 100 kb; internal TTAGGG-like tracts sit at duplicon boundaries; six subterminal duplicon families plus six single-copy segments account for all telomere-adjacent sequence.
Updated, gap-filled subtelomere assemblies and multiread-mapping annotation pipeline (Riethman lab), with CTCF/cohesin site mapping; the previous reference resource for human subtelomeres.
Review: subterminal sequences linked to cis-acting allele-specific telomere length regulation and highly variable subtelomeric allele structures.
Review of subtelomeric copy-number variation and its potential dosage and position effects.
Seminal review defining subtelomeres as patchworks of duplicated blocks shared among non-homologous ends and arguing for frequent recent exchange.

Subtelomeric patchworks arose recently through repeated translocations between ends; breakpoint analysis indicates non-homologous end-joining predominates; half of known subtelomeric sequence is human-specific. Central prior for terminal transfer mechanism.

OR-containing subtelomeric block present at 3q, 15q, 19p in all 45 individuals and polymorphically at 11 further ends with population-variable frequencies: an early population view of terminal allele polymorphism.
SNP and Alu analysis of 181 copies of an OR subtelomeric block from 12 ends shows recent interactions between non-homologous ends.
Copies of subtelomeric OR-A vary in number and location among humans; most are intact and transcribed.
WASH genes are the most terminally located subtelomeric genes; defines a new WASP subclass.
16p13.3 terminal region shows stable length polymorphism up to 260 kb among 47 chromosomes: discrete terminal structural alleles that segregate as Mendelian alleles.
First full sequence (284 kb) of a human telomeric region (16p) from TTAGGG to unique DNA.
Telomere-associated DNA at four ends: repeat families shared among ends and polymorphism near telomeres.
Direct cloning of human telomere-associated DNA; telomere-adjacent sequences variable and shared among ends.
Sequences of 4p, 16p, 22q ends: degenerate internal TTAGGG divide distal (short shared patches) from proximal (10-40 kb homology to few ends) subdomains.

A telomere-plus-adjacent DNA unit is present on ~6% of 16q and 2% of 16p chromosomes and has relocated at least once; relocation involved the adjacent DNA. Earliest direct example of a polymorphic, transposed terminal allele.
FISH with subtelomeric cosmids: large segmental polymorphisms at proterminal regions, consistent with both reciprocal translocation and homology-based spreading among non-homologous ends.
Subtelomeric cosmid hybridises to 16 sites on 12 chromosomes, 10 of them variable between individuals.
14q subtelomeric polymorphisms and elevated, male-biased recombination near the 14q telomere.
15q subtelomere formed by fission in the great-ape ancestor and subsequently exchanged material with other ends, including a >=200 kb transfer to 4q in chimp/gorilla.
Xp/Yp telomere-adjacent segmental duplication with DXYS14 minisatellite; mutation processes driving turnover of a telomere-adjacent duplication.
7E olfactory receptor pseudogenes in segmental duplications show complex evolution including ectopic exchange.
Survey of 40 constitutional rearrangements: frequency of chromosome healing versus interstitial telomeres at junctions.
Truncated 16p in alpha-thalassaemia healed by direct TTAGGG addition: first human telomere healing.
16p break stabilised by acquiring a new telomere through Alu-Alu recombination with another subtelomere: homology-mediated terminal replacement in a germline allele.
Apparent terminal deletions are cryptic subtelomeric translocations; telomere capture stabilises broken chromosomes.
der(1)t(1;1)(p36;q44) breakpoints lack homology/LCRs, suggesting BIR-mediated telomere capture rather than NAHR.
8p inv-dup stabilised by capture of an 18q telomere.
8p inv-dup-del with telomere capture from 8q.
Inv-dup-del cases: telomere capture is a frequent stabilisation mechanism of terminal deletions.
Terminal 18q deletions stabilised by neotelomeres (healing or capture).
Review of chromosome healing and telomere capture in radiation-induced breakage.

Junction sequencing of 21 pathogenic subtelomeric rearrangements: NHEJ, NAHR between interspersed repeats and replication-based signatures; breakage hotspots at 9q and 22q. Mechanistic baseline for junction features.
Long-read cancer genomes reveal neotelomeres and telomere-spanning arm fusions; shows long reads can type terminal rearrangement junctions.
Korean long-read assemblies: 19 large subtelomeric SVs examined for repair signatures, inferring mechanisms of subtelomere SV formation.
Yeast: one-ended DSB repaired by BIR into a distant chromosome end with 72 bp homology gives nonreciprocal translocations and telomere capture. Mechanistic model for one-way terminal transfer.
MMBIR model: complex CNVs with 2-5 bp microhomology junctions arise by template switching during break-induced replication.
BIR and telomerase-independent telomere maintenance require Pol32.
Review: BIR repairs one-ended breaks including eroded telomeres and causes LOH and nonreciprocal translocations.
Review of BIR: migrating bubble, conservative synthesis, mutagenic and rearrangement-prone.
Break-induced telomere synthesis underlies ALT in human cells.
Yeast: subtelomeric DSBs repaired by gene conversion or BIR depending on distance from the end, resection and chromatin.
Yeast: BIR encountering an ITS frequently terminates and forms an ectopic telomere; links ITS to terminal-replacement end points.
ITSs raise gross chromosomal rearrangement rates via several mechanisms in yeast.
Telomeric amplicons generated by MMBIR in cis in yeast, appended at chromosome ends.
Fission yeast HAATI: RNAi-dependent nonreciprocal translocations at eroding ends.
Review: telomere loss, subtelomeric DSB sensitivity and the consequences (BFB, nonreciprocal translocation) in cancer.
Review: subtelomeric regions are sensitive to DSBs and deficient in repair, driving telomere loss in cancer.
Shortest telomeres trigger fusions and karyotype evolution in transformed cells.
Single-molecule analysis of telomere fusions defines the critical fusogenic telomere length.
Classifies human ITSs into short, subtelomeric and fusion classes; short ITSs inserted at DSB repair sites in the germline.
Comparative primate analysis: ITSs inserted suddenly at DSB sites during primate evolution (40-6 Mya), not by expansion.
ITSs in primates and rodents consistent with telomerase-mediated insertion during DSB repair.
Review of heterochromatic and short ITSs and their evolutionary origin.
Review of telomeric repeats and ITSs: structure, instability and maintenance.
Length polymorphism of four human ITSs, including a subtelomeric 6p ITS.
Human 2q13 contains head-to-head telomere arrays from the ancestral telomere-telomere fusion.
Structure of the 2q13-q14.1 fusion site and paralogous subtelomere-derived blocks elsewhere.
Rearrangements producing interstitial telomeric sequences at junctions: types and stability.
Recombination at interstitial telomere-like sequences promotes instability in hamster cells.
ITSs are not located exactly at primate inversion breakpoints.
FISH survey of ITSs in primates.
Southern data indicating exchange of D4Z4 3.3 kb units between 4q35 and 10q26.
208 Dutch donors: ~20% carry translocated 4q/10q D4Z4 arrays; model of subtelomeric plasticity.
10q and 4q telomeres share sequence beyond D4Z4, suggesting common origin.
4qA and 4qB distal variants; FSHD exclusively associated with 4qA.
Specific 4q35 sequence variants define FSHD-permissive haplotypes; D4Z4 rearrangement occurs mostly intrachromosomally.

HapMap/HGDP 4q/10q haplotype network: all 4q/10q subtelomeres trace to only four discrete transfer events, all pre-dating out-of-Africa; mixed haplotypes are intermediates. Key precedent that subtelomere exchange alleles are few and old.
FSHD requires D4Z4 contraction on a permissive 4qA haplotype with a DUX4 polyadenylation signal.
4qter and 10qter D4Z4 regions evolved independently under different constraints.
Ape comparison of the 4q35.2 region: evolutionary remodelling.
4q;10q translocation frequencies differ among populations.
Molecular combing resolves complex 4q/10q subtelomere configurations.
Complex 4q35/10q26 rearrangements in FSHD diagnostics.
Engineered exchange of 4q and 10q subtelomeric regions reverts the FSHD genotype and phenotype, demonstrating functional consequence of terminal swapping.
T2T re-analysis of D4Z4-like repeats beyond 4q35/10q26.
Preprint: long-read D4Z4 genetic/epigenetic architecture in FSHD and controls.
Preprint: HiFi-based resolution of D4Z4 arrays.
Benchmark of long-read approaches for the FSHD locus.

Complete assemblies of three Robertsonian chromosomes reveal a common breakpoint.
Preprint on great-ape acrocentric origins and interchromosomal exchange.
Preprint: biobank genotyping of Robertsonian translocations.
Perspective on acrocentric short arms.
Review of acrocentric p-arm biology.
Model of Robertsonian formation.

CHM13 improves variant calling across 3,202 genomes.
